paper.title: Hierarchy-boosted funnel learning for identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes a hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework that integrates unsupervised and supervised learning to efficiently identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL), circumventing large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations. It uses unsupervised clustering on descriptors to narrow the search space, performs low-cost high-throughput calculations (HTC) on selected clusters to build a labeled local database, trains a CatBoost classifier for direct prediction, and conducts interpretable analysis to uncover structure-property relationships—particularly a new descriptor Lmin governing structural anharmonicity.

tasks.task_name_raw: identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
tasks.objective: efficiently discover semiconductors exhibiting ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL) for thermoelectric applications
input_requirements: descriptors derived from Magpie and Voronoi tessellations
output_goal: list of candidate semiconductors with ultralow κL

evidence.text: Here, we propose a novel hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework, which is successfully applied to identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL).
We then apply this HiBoFL framework to efﬁciently identify semiconductors with ultralow κL as shown in Fig. 1b.

As a compelling demonstration, this framework has been successfully applied to identify semiconductors with ultralow κL, which circumvents large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations without clear objectives.

evidence.text: Ultimately, through excluding the materials containing hydrogen, lanthanides, and actinides, and conducting structural analysis, we further obtain 2675 three-dimensional (3D) crystal structures without calculation errors. These materials constitute the ﬁrst-level dataset for our in-depth investigations.

stages.stage_name_raw: unsupervised learning to identify problem-specific clusters with similar κL
stages.stage_goal: group materials into clusters based on compositional and structural similarity to prioritize those likely exhibiting low κL
stage_output: problem-specific clusters C1 and C2 (704 materials)

evidence.text: K-means clustering41,42 is then employed to identify materials with similar κL, which is visualized in a low-dimensional space using t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE)43, and problem-speciﬁc clusters are selected based on similarity design rules to form the second-level dataset.

Since the materials with a high likelihood of possessing relatively low κL tend to group into the two clusters of C1 and C2, the exploration scope for ﬁnding materials with low κL is reduced from 2675 materials to 704 materials, narrowing by approximately three-quarters. As a result, these two problem-speciﬁc clusters (C1 and C2) further constitute our second-level dataset.

stages.stage_name_raw: high-throughput calculation (HTC) of κPET on problem-specific clusters
stages.stage_goal: assign approximate κL labels to materials in C1 and C2 using the low-cost PET empirical model
stage_output: local database of 661 materials with κPET values at 300 K

evidence.text: We use the phonon-elasticity-thermal (PET) model44 to perform low-cost HTC on the materials in the second-level dataset, establishing a local database based on the HTC results.

stages.stage_name_raw: labeling materials as ultralow or non-ultralow κL based on κPET threshold
stages.stage_goal: generate binary classification labels for supervised learning using κPET ≤2 W/mK as cutoff

evidence.text: Here, materials with κPET not exceeding 2 W/mK are labeled as 1, which are considered to possess ultralow κL; otherwise, they are labeled as 0, signifying non-ultralow κL.

stages.stage_name_raw: training CatBoost classifier on labeled local database
stages.stage_goal: train robust supervised classification model to predict ultralow κL directly from descriptors

evidence.text: We perform ensemble learning on the labeled local database for directly classifying ultralow κL, training a robust CatBoost classifier45.

stages.stage_goal: assess classification accuracy and robustness using standard metrics

evidence.text: As a result, the performances of the optimal CatBoost classiﬁcation model are characterized by the ROC curve and the confusion matrix (Fig. 6b), showing its great ability in classifying semiconductors with ultralow κL due to the high ROC AUC (0.94), accuracy (0.90), precision (0.89), recall (0.90) and F1-score (0.89).

stages.stage_name_raw: screening candidate materials with ultralow κL for in-depth mechanism analysis
stages.stage_goal: select top-performing candidates from HTC and model predictions for first-principles validation
stage_output: Cs2SnSe3 and Cs2GeSe3 selected for BTE calculation

evidence.text: To further validate the results and conduct in-depth analysis of the phonon thermal transport mechanisms, we calculate more precise κL values according to ﬁrst-principles derived force constants and Boltzmann transport theory for the unreported materials Cs2SnSe3 and Cs2GeSe3, which are screened out based on the formula type ranking among the materials with the lowest κPET values.

stages.stage_goal: verify ultralow κL predictions and reveal underlying phonon transport mechanisms
stage_output: precise κL values (<0.25 W/mK at 300 K)

stages.stage_name_raw: interpretable analysis using SHAP to link descriptors to κL mechanisms

evidence.text: The interpretable analysis of the pre-trained model based on the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method46–48 further reveals the inﬂuence of important descriptors on ultralow κL. A new factor capable of signiﬁcantly reducing κL via enhancing structural anharmonicity is discovered, eventually building a bridge between the ML model interpretability and ﬁrst-principles analysis.
